title: Underpayment Addition on Medicaid Plan Appeals — Insurance Coverage & Claims Variance Note
content:
**Variance note — Insurance Coverage & Claims, Medicaid Managed Care Plan plan appeals.**

A Medicaid allowed ratio is the plan's payment plus the member responsibility it assigned, divided by that payment plus the contractual adjustment plus that member responsibility; the claim's own ratio takes these amounts over the claim's lines and the coverage's twelve-month ratio over every such line on the coverage within the last twelve months.

The plan appeal's **underpayment gap**, figured only where the claim has a paid line, is the coverage's twelve-month Medicaid allowed ratio less the claim's own ratio, in percentage points. The claim's **paid-line charges** are the plan's payment plus the contractual adjustment plus the member responsibility on the claim.

The plan appeal's **underpayment addition** is:

- the whole gap applied to the paid-line charges (the gap divided by one hundred, times the paid-line charges) where the gap exceeds the plan variance tolerance of **5 percentage points**;
- the part of the gap above the plan variance floor of **2 percentage points** applied to the paid-line charges where the gap exceeds the floor but not the tolerance;
- nothing otherwise, including where the claim has no paid line.

## Hypothetical figures (paid-line charges 500.00 USD)

| Twelve-month ratio | Claim's own ratio | Gap | Addition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.86 | 0.80 | 6 points | 6 divided by one hundred, times 500.00: 30.00 |
| 0.85 | 0.80 | 5 points | 5 less 2, divided by one hundred, times 500.00: 15.00 |
| 0.83 | 0.80 | 3 points | 1 divided by one hundred, times 500.00: 5.00 |
| 0.82 | 0.80 | 2 points | Nothing |
